edits.new: Each entry has a `subject` naming a topic and a `context` helping interpret the subject.
edits.old: Each entry has a `subject` naming a topic and a `context` helping interpret its scope.

edits.new: The selected subject establishes the topic, its level of abstraction and its expressed restrictions. Use the full post, its context and the surrounding hierarchy to resolve its intended sense, references and named identity. Preserve the full scope of that subject in the chosen sense. Distinguish resolving a different sense from restricting the same category to the post's particular kind, use, purpose, state or circumstance. An example does not make those details category-wide conditions. The full post is the definitive evidence for facts about particular people, things and events; subject, context and hierarchy text cannot independently establish unsupported facts.
edits.old: The selected subject identifies the topic to define. Its context and the surrounding hierarchy guide interpretation. The full post is the definitive evidence for facts about what it describes; subject, context and hierarchy text cannot independently establish unsupported facts.

edits.new: The hierarchy records intended generalizations and narrower topics. Its relationships guide interpretation; they do not establish factual claims.
edits.old: The hierarchy indicates levels of abstraction and relationships among the topics illustrated in this post.

edits.new: Distinguish what the subject identifies from which information belongs under it. Examine roles, purposes and states expressed by the selected subject or required by its intended sense. Decide whether they identify the topic, limit the information covered, or do both. State each defining condition directly, including whether it characterizes a kind or must hold for a particular example. Details that merely describe the post's example do not restrict the category. A broad condition can define membership without listing every possible participant or use. Record and resolve an ambiguity when competing interpretations of the selected subject admit different information, not merely because another restriction could be added.
edits.old: Distinguish what the subject identifies from which information belongs under it. Examine roles, purposes and states suggested by the input: decide whether they identify the topic, limit the information covered, or do both. When a participant's, material's or product's role or intended use changes membership, state the qualifying condition directly rather than leaving it implicit in a familiar name. Decide whether each condition characterizes a kind or must hold for the particular example. A broad condition can define membership without listing every possible participant or use; a narrower example does not silently restrict it. Record and resolve an ambiguity when competing interpretations suggested by the input admit different information, not merely because another restriction could be added.

edits.new: Resolve each ambiguity using the selected subject, its context, the original branch and the post. Preserve the subject's expressed restrictions and named identity, including all explicitly named alternatives and parts. Use ancestors and descendants to help interpret its sense and level of abstraction. A relationship cannot add a restriction missing from the selected subject or justify discarding part of it to make it fit. A description requiring several parts together may narrow the topic of a required part; the other parts need not be instances of that part's kind or action. Decide whether multiple named parts must be described together or are alternatives admitted independently. Co-mention alone does not settle this. Preserve the restrictions the selected subject applies to each admitted alternative. If a coherent interpretation of the selected subject cannot be justified, record the ambiguity as unresolved.
edits.old: Resolve each ambiguity using the selected subject, its context, the original branch and the post. Preserve the subject's stated boundaries and any named identity, including all explicitly named alternatives and parts of the topic. Do not discard an alternative or part solely to make the topic fit its parent. Interpret each parent-child link as an intended narrowing of the information topic, subject to the post's factual evidence. When a parent is present, choose a supported meaning of the selected topic within its parent's scope, retaining any general role, purpose or state that defines that scope. Generalize across kinds or applications satisfying those conditions; a descendant's more specific application does not remove a condition from the selected category. An ancestor's incidental details do not automatically define membership. Check whether all information covered by the selected meaning preserves the parent's required subject matter, role, purpose and state. A description requiring several parts together may narrow the topic of a required part; the other parts need not be instances of that part's kind or action. Decide whether multiple named parts must be described together or are alternatives admitted independently. Co-mention alone does not settle this. For alternatives, every admitted alternative must meet the parent's requirements. If this check fails, or preserving the relationship requires discarding part of the selected topic or adding unsupported facts, record that conflict as unresolved.

edits.new: When the selected subject admits competing senses or defining boundaries, make a justified choice that preserves its level of abstraction and expressed restrictions. Do not substitute a broader or narrower topic or combine competing interpretations to avoid deciding.
edits.old: When more than one abstraction is reasonable, make a justified choice. Do not automatically choose the broadest or narrowest interpretation, or combine competing interpretations to avoid deciding.

edits.new: express a restriction stated by the selected subject or required by its intended sense directly as a condition of that activity.
edits.old: express an input-supported restriction on those kinds directly as a condition of that activity.
